_note: Regime anchors for the record-to-parcel cardinality guard (scripts/check_value_anchors.py). Bands, not equalities: assessed values move every reassessment. See docs/FINDINGS_lot_dedupe.md and docs/FINDINGS_denominator_cardinality.md.
_bands_are_per_anchor: ⚠️ THESE BANDS ARE NO LONGER UNIFORM AND `--write-baseline` WOULD FLATTEN THEM. That flag applies ONE global --tolerance (default 0.5) to every anchor, which is exactly what this file stopped doing on 2026-08-05. If you re-pin with it, re-apply the split below by hand or the drift guard silently loosens back to ±50%.
_why_two_widths: Set 2026-08-05 from the first real variance data: every anchor value the guard has logged in CI since it shipped (5 runs, but only 3 INDEPENDENT data changes — 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-05 committed status.json only, so their readings re-measure unchanged input). FOUR anchors were effectively frozen across that window (dup_parcel_points constant at 33; dedupe_effect_pct 0.01% spread; dup_parcel_value_frac 0.11%; lot_needle_ratio 0.00%) and were tightened 2x, to ±25% of the latest reading. TWO were NOT tightened because they looked like they were TRENDING — that trend was falsified 2026-09-03, but they stay at ±50% anyway; see _ineligible_pair_was_NOT_drifting. ⚠️ THE '3 INDEPENDENT DATA CHANGES' CLAIM ABOVE IS WRONG (2026-09-03): that window held SIX runs and only TWO distinct states, so the flatness that earned the ±25% rested on two observations, not three. ⚠️ IT HAS SINCE BEEN EARNED HONESTLY AND THE BANDS NEED NO CHANGE — 8 further CI states through 2026-09-02 keep dedupe_effect_pct in 0.040806-0.0408324, dup_parcel_value_frac in 0.00309363-0.00309689 and dup_parcel_points at a flat 33, all far inside ±25%. lot_needle_ratio left that group on 2026-09-01 (the 50 m grid) and is at ±50%.
_why_only_25_percent: ⚠️ NOT tightened to the observed spread (~0.1%), deliberately. The guard exists mainly for the January year-roll (docs/RUNBOOK.md), and NO OBSERVATION ACROSS A YEAR-ROLL EXISTS YET — the guard shipped 2026-07-28. Three weekly observations say nothing about how these move on reassessment, so ±25% buys a real 2x tightening while leaving room for the event the guard was built for. Revisit after the first January roll, which is the observation that would justify going tighter.
_ineligible_pair_was_NOT_drifting: ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-03 — THE TREND THIS FIELD ASSERTED IS FALSIFIED. It claimed ineligible_points and ineligible_value_frac moved 'on EVERY independent data change, monotonically upward, with no reversal' (56 -> 58 -> 60 and 0.00517 -> 0.00575 -> 0.00633 across 2026-08-01/08-03/08-04), that value_frac had consumed ~72% of its band, and that it would breach in 2-3 more moves. It was written from a 3-observation window, and the TODO item it spawned said exactly that: 'Confirm the trend continues before treating the slope as real.' ⚠️ THE CONFIRMING DATA EXISTED ALL ALONG — every refresh run logs both anchors against a FRESH pull, so `gh run view <id> --log | grep ineligible_` over the run list is the whole series. IT REVERSED AND WENT FLAT: points 56 (08-01, 08-02, 08-03 05:17) -> 60 (08-03 11:19, 08-04, 08-05) -> 56 (08-10) -> 57 (08-17 .. 08-31) -> 58 (09-02); value_frac 0.00517178 -> 0.00632732 -> 0.00516634 -> 0.00516946 -> 0.00515087 -> 0.00515159 -> 0.00515519. ⚠️ AND THE MIDDLE OF THE ORIGINAL THREE WAS NEVER OBSERVED — the 58 / 0.00575 was an INTERPOLATION matching no CI run (see OBSERVED_IN_CI in tests/test_check_value_anchors.py, where it sat as a pinned row until 2026-09-03; all five of its anchors were midpoints of the rows either side). The window held SIX runs but only TWO distinct data states, the step falling between the 05:17 and 11:19 runs of 08-03. So the 'monotonic trend' was ONE STEP with an invented midpoint, and the blip it belonged to was gone by 08-10. Across the 8 independent pulls since 08-10 the pair has moved ~0.3%. ineligible_value_frac sits at 49.4% of its band (0.00515519 in 0.002593-0.007779) — dead centre, nowhere near breaching — and is deliberately NOT re-pinned, being already within 0.6% of its centre. ⚠️ STILL DO NOT TIGHTEN EITHER TO ±25%: that width is earned by flatness ACROSS A JANUARY YEAR-ROLL, which still has zero observations (see _why_only_25_percent). Three flat weeks is not that evidence.
_ineligible_points_repinned_2026_09_03: ⚠️ RE-PINNED TO 29-87 (centre 58, the 2026-09-02 CI reading), REVERTING A RE-PIN THAT WAS MADE AGAINST STALE LOCAL DATA. The 2026-09-02 note claimed 'reading 85 ... 84 by 2026-09-02, which had reached the band ceiling EXACTLY and would have fired on the next weekly publish on its own', and widened 28-84 -> 42.5-127.5. IT WOULD NOT HAVE FIRED: CI that same day (refresh run 33648662596, which does a fresh scripts/download_data.py pull) read 58 — comfortably inside 28-84. The 84/85 was an artifact of this box's data/raw/, where Property_Info__Current_Calendar_Year_.csv was dated 2026-07-06 against a 2026-08-09 assessment file: a stale, MISMATCHED pair, and majority-null lot_size is exactly what such a mismatch distorts. ⚠️ THE COST WAS REAL — the ceiling moved 84 -> 127.5, halving this guard's sensitivity in its own declared DANGEROUS direction (growth) to accommodate a number the published pipeline never produced. The floor move was harmless: below-band on a high-danger anchor is 'benign', warn-only, and never reds the publish. ⚠️ ONLY TRUST THESE TWO ANCHORS AGAINST A FRESH PULL. check_value_anchors.py now prints the vintage of every raw file it reads and warns when they are stale or mismatched, so a local run says so out loud instead of quietly handing you a re-pin.
